verdict.summary: You can create a Notion public connection yourself, and any Notion user can authorize it through OAuth with no review. Notion only reviews Marketplace listings, and listing is optional. The main trap is that installation scope ('Any workspace' or 'Selected workspaces only') is set once when you create the connection and can't be changed later.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min (add a few hours if you later prepare a Marketplace listing)
verdict.approval_wait: none for OAuth installs; 5-10 business days for an optional Marketplace listing review

gates.name: Public connection (your own workspace)
gates.unlocks: You can authorize your own Notion account through your own client ID and secret, and use the pages you pick in the page picker.
limits: Access only reaches the pages you select in the page picker (and their children)

Default rate limit of about 3 requests/second per integration per workspace (community source); a reported change from 9 Sept 2026 sets 180 requests/min on most plans and 600/min on Business and Enterprise

gates.name: Public connection, Selected workspaces only
gates.unlocks: Users in the workspaces you choose can each complete the OAuth flow and get their own token.
limits: Not eligible for the Marketplace, and the installation scope can't be changed later
Each workspace member has to authorize separately
No official install cap was found

gates.name: Public connection, Any workspace (optionally listed on the Marketplace)
gates.unlocks: Any Notion user can install the connection through your OAuth link. A Marketplace listing adds discoverability inside Notion.
limits: A Marketplace listing needs a Notion security review and listing review; plain OAuth installs do not
Listings can be rejected for brand/trademark issues, quality concerns, or failing baseline connection criteria; you can revise and resubmit
Reviewed connections may be able to request higher rate limits (community source)
gates.time_to_reach: Immediate for OAuth installs; 5-10 business days for a listing review response

steps.title: Decide whether you need your own app
steps.detail: Composio's managed Notion OAuth works for testing. Register your own public connection if you want your own app name and identity shown to users, your own redirect, or a Marketplace listing. Use a public connection (OAuth), not an internal connection, because other users need to install it.

steps.title: Sign in to the Notion Developer portal
steps.detail: Sign in with your normal Notion login. notion.so/my-integrations redirects to the same portal. Use a workspace you can administer as the development workspace.
gotchas: Notion's docs say you must be a workspace owner to create an internal connection. They don't say whether the same applies to public connections.

steps.title: Choose the installation scope carefully
steps.detail: Pick 'Any workspace' if anyone outside your workspaces might ever install the app or you might list it on the Marketplace. Pick 'Selected workspaces only' only for a closed audience. You can't change this after the connection is created.
gotchas: If you start with 'Selected workspaces only' and later want a Marketplace listing, you'll have to create a new connection, which comes with a new client ID and secret.

steps.title: Create the public connection
steps.detail: Go to Build > Public connections > Create new connection. Fill in the name, development workspace, redirect URI, installation scope and capabilities. If a guide shows the connection defaulting to Internal, switch it to Public so you get OAuth credentials.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Redirect URIs must include a protocol and can't contain fragments, relative paths, wildcards or a public IP address (community source).

steps.title: Request only the capabilities you need
steps.detail: Map your agent's actions to Notion capabilities: read content, update content, insert content, read/insert comments, and the user information level. Request the smallest set that works, because workspace admins are more likely to approve fewer capabilities.
gotchas: If you change capabilities later, every existing user has to re-authenticate.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and secret into Composio
steps.detail: Open the connection's Configuration tab and copy the OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret. Create a Notion auth config in Composio that uses your own credentials, and leave scopes empty.

values.label: Scopes
values.value: (none; access comes from capabilities and the page picker)

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection through Composio. Notion's authorize request uses client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and owner=user. In the page picker, select the pages the agent should reach, then check that the token exchange returns an access token, a refresh token and a workspace_id.
gotchas: The agent only sees the pages you pick and their children. If API calls return empty results or not-found errors, re-run the flow and share more pages.
Refreshing a token returns a new refresh token too. Store the new one every time you refresh.

steps.title: Share the connect flow with other users
steps.detail: Send invited users (Selected workspaces) or anyone (Any workspace) through your Composio connect link. Each user gets a token for their own workspace, and each workspace member has to authorize separately.

steps.title: Optionally add a template and watch connection health
steps.detail: You can set a public Notion page as a template that's offered during the auth flow, in the connection's distribution settings. Use the Health tab in the Developer portal to track requests, failures and rate-limit warnings over the last 24 hours.

steps.title: Optional: draft and submit a Marketplace listing
steps.detail: For an 'Any workspace' connection, draft the name, description, category, tags, images and logo. Save the listing as a draft, then submit it from Listings > Connections. A person has to do the final submit in the portal.
gotchas: Listing requires a Notion security review. Its exact requirements were not documented in the research.
Avoid using Notion's brand or trademarks in your name and logo; trademark issues are a named rejection reason.

steps.title: Wait for Notion's listing review
steps.detail: Notion replies by email within 5-10 business days. If they ask for changes, revise the listing and resubmit. OAuth installs keep working while the listing is under review.

requirements.item: Notion account and a development workspace
requirements.detail: Your developer account is your normal Notion login. Creating an internal connection requires workspace owner rights; whether public connections need the same is unconfirmed.

requirements.item: Redirect URI registered on the connection
requirements.detail: It must match the Composio callback exactly. If you configure more than one redirect URI, the token request has to include redirect_uri.
The token exchange uses HTTP Basic auth built from the client ID and secret. PKCE support was not confirmed.
Each refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token. Store both every time.
Plan for per-connection limits (180 requests/min on most plans, 600/min on Business and Enterprise, as reported from 9 Sept 2026) plus per-workspace limits.
Only connections with this scope can be listed on the Marketplace, and the scope can't be changed later.
Name, description, category, tags, images and logo, plus a Notion security review before the listing goes live. All of this applies only if you list on the Marketplace.

scopes.effect: Lets the agent read the pages the user shares in the page picker. Notion has no OAuth scope strings or documented sensitivity tiers.
Needed for write actions. Every extra capability makes workspace admins less likely to approve the install, and changing capabilities later forces users to re-authenticate.
Request these only if the agent works with comments. Adding them later forces users to re-authenticate.
Controls how much user information, such as email, the connection can see. Choose the lowest level that works.

blockers.symptom: Your connection doesn't appear as eligible for a Marketplace listing
blockers.cause: It was created with 'Selected workspaces only' installation scope, which can't be changed.
blockers.fix: Create a new public connection with 'Any workspace' scope and move users over to it, which means swapping in new credentials in Composio.

blockers.cause: Brand/trademark issues, quality concerns, or failing baseline connection criteria.
blockers.fix: Address the feedback in Notion's email, follow the Connection Gallery Best Practices, and resubmit.

blockers.symptom: Existing users lose access after an update
blockers.cause: The connection's capabilities were changed, which forces users to re-authenticate.
blockers.fix: Settle on capabilities before launch, and ask users to reconnect after any change.

blockers.symptom: API calls return nothing or object-not-found for pages the user expects
blockers.cause: The user didn't select those pages in the OAuth page picker.
blockers.fix: Have the user re-run the connect flow, or share the pages with the connection.

blockers.cause: Per-connection or per-workspace rate limits were exceeded.
blockers.fix: Add backoff and spread requests out. Check the Health tab for rate-limit warnings.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed Notion OAuth for testing. It has no scopes because Notion access comes from capabilities and the page picker. Switch to your own public connection when you want your own app name in the consent screen, your own capability choices, or a Marketplace listing (which requires 'Any workspace' scope). Paste the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config as the Redirect URI. The research found two different Composio callback paths, so copy it from the auth config instead of typing it from memory.

evidence.claim: Public connections are created in the Developer portal via Build > Public connections > Create new connection, with name, workspace, redirect URIs, installation scope and capabilities.
evidence.quote: Click **Create new connection** and fill in the required fields, including:

evidence.claim: Changing capabilities forces users to re-authenticate.
evidence.quote: users will need to re-authenticate with a connection if the capabilities are changed

evidence.claim: Users select which pages the connection can access in a page picker.
evidence.quote: Users can select which pages to give the connection access to

evidence.claim: A security review is required before Marketplace listing, not for using a public connection.
evidence.quote: Public connections must undergo a Notion security review before being listed on the Marketplace.

evidence.claim: Only 'Any workspace' public connections can be listed; a listing needs name, description, category, tags, images and logo.
evidence.quote: Only public connections with an installation scope of **Any workspace** can be listed on the Marketplace.

evidence.claim: Notion reviews every listing submission.
evidence.quote: The Notion team reviews every listing submission.

evidence.claim: Listing review responses arrive by email within 5-10 business days.
evidence.quote: expect to hear back from our team within 5-10 business days via email.

evidence.claim: Rejection reasons include brand/trademark issues and quality concerns; resubmission is allowed.
evidence.quote: Connections are rejected for various reasons, from brand/trademark issues to quality concerns

evidence.claim: Notion references a Connection Gallery Best Practices document from the listing guide.
evidence.quote: Notion Connection Gallery Best Practices

evidence.claim: Public connections work without a Marketplace listing.
evidence.quote: Public connections work independently of Marketplace listings.

evidence.claim: Redirect URIs can't contain fragments, relative paths, wildcards or a public IP address.
evidence.quote: It can’t contain URL fragments, relative paths or wildcards, and can’t be a public IP address.

evidence.claim: The OAuth client ID and secret are on the connection's Configuration tab.
evidence.quote: visit the **Configuration** tab to retrieve your **OAuth client ID** and **OAuth client secret**.

evidence.claim: Redirect URIs are configured when the public connection is created.
evidence.quote: Redirect URI(s) for the OAuth flow

evidence.claim: The default rate limit is 3 requests/second for public integrations without approval.
evidence.quote: This applies to internal integrations (created with a shared secret) and public integrations that haven’t gone through the approval process.

evidence.claim: Reviewed integrations can reportedly request up to 100 requests/second for Enterprise workspaces.
evidence.quote: The documentation claims you can request up to 100 requests per second for Enterprise workspaces.

evidence.claim: From 9 Sept 2026: 600 requests/min on Business and Enterprise, 180/min on other plans, per connection.
evidence.quote: 600 requests per minute on Business and Enterprise plans, and 180 requests per minute on all other plans.

evidence.claim: Rate limits also apply per workspace, in addition to per connection.
evidence.quote: Notion API now applies rate limits per workspace in addition to per-connection limits, scaled to workspace plan.

evidence.claim: Connections have a Health tab showing requests, failures and rate-limit warnings.
evidence.quote: Internal and public connections now have a Health tab in the Developer portal.

evidence.claim: Creating an internal connection requires being a workspace owner.
evidence.quote: You are required to be a workspace owner to create a connection.

evidence.claim: The developer portal uses your Notion login; notion.so/my-integrations redirects to it.
evidence.quote: Notion JavaScript must be enabled in order to use Notion.

evidence.claim: Public connections use OAuth 2.0; internal connections use a static token for one workspace.
evidence.quote: Public connections use OAuth 2.0 for authentication.

evidence.claim: A new integration may default to Internal and must be made Public for OAuth.
evidence.quote: You need to make it **Public** to initiate an OAuth flow with users.

evidence.claim: No OAuth scope is required by default for Notion integrations.
evidence.quote: No OAuth scope is required by default for Notion integrations.

evidence.claim: n8n says public integrations need a Notion security review before publishing, with company name and website requested.
evidence.quote: They require a Notion security review before publishing.

evidence.claim: Public connections can offer a template page during the auth flow, set in distribution settings.
evidence.quote: Public connections offer the option of providing a public Notion page to use as a template during the auth flow.

evidence.claim: Installation scope (Any workspace vs Selected workspaces only) is set at creation and can't be changed.
evidence.quote: Installation scope is set once, at creation time, and can't be changed afterward.

evidence.claim: The authorize request uses client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and owner=user.
evidence.quote: Always use `user`.

evidence.claim: Token exchange is a POST to /v1/oauth/token using HTTP Basic auth, with redirect_uri required in some cases.
evidence.quote: The request is authorized using HTTP Basic Authentication.

evidence.claim: Refreshing returns a new access token and a new refresh token; no lifetime is stated.
evidence.quote: Refreshing an access token will generate a new access token and a new refresh token.

evidence.claim: Each authorizing user gets their own token scoped to their workspace.
evidence.quote: each user who authorizes the connection receives their own access token, scoped to their workspace.

evidence.claim: Permissions come from capabilities; fewer capabilities make admin approval more likely.
evidence.quote: The fewer capabilities you request, the more likely a workspace admin will be able to install your connection.

open_questions: How long access tokens last before expiring is not documented; only the refresh flow is.
PKCE support is unconfirmed; the token exchange uses a client secret with HTTP Basic auth.
What the security review checks and how long it takes, separate from the 5-10 business-day listing response, is not documented.
Whether you must be a workspace owner to create a public connection (documented for internal connections only).
No official install cap was found for unreviewed public connections or for 'Selected workspaces only' connections.
Official per-plan rate limits rely on community mirrors; the Request limits reference page and the Connection Gallery Best Practices page were not retrieved.
Which Composio callback URL (api/v1/auth-apps/add or api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback) applies; copy the one shown in your auth config.
